families.name: Masthead
families.summary: The head of a page or app. The header is a glass panel with a large caption: number left in the tone, title right, an etched rule under both. --bar is the one-line top bar, the client's round logo first (__mark); --split puts the caption and the tools in two pills with the page between them. Three layouts of it share that panel and content: centred (as is), --app-inline (a one-line readout after the lead, etched rules between items) and --app-tiles (each item a sidebar row tile with its cube, the tools past an etched rule). A grid of option tiles with data-fh-backdrop-select picks the backdrop and remembers it. Glass over it frosts by --fh-frost (0–1), a theme token; a range with data-fh-frost-select dials it live and remembers it. The frost line frosts the art behind a hero from a line down, with a hard edge: --fh-backdrop-frost-from places the line.

families.markup:
Why it matters

Most systems fail at the seams, not the center

Each tool works on its own. The cost shows up where data crosses from one to the next: re-keyed orders, stale reports, follow-ups nobody owns.

The approach

  • Map every hand-off between systems
  • Fix the model before adding automation
  • Instrument it so problems surface first

families.name: Metric tiles
families.summary: Drawn from data by metrics.js: the figure, its delta, a ratio and the people come from the data display contract's metric context, so an amount reads $48.2K with its change, a share is a ring, a bar or a meter against its target, and a team is a count beside its avatars. One fact per tile: label with an icon, the value, a line under it and where it came from. As many across as fit. Add an fh-progress for a share done, --needed for a fact still to fill in, or make the tile an <a> to open its area. --spread puts the label and description at the top and the value at the bottom, with a wide gap. __row holds avatars, counts and chips. __more is an etched line with a chevron: open, the tile grows in place and shows its detail, so the chevron stays under the pointer; use --full when the detail needs room. __delta shows the change (data-trend; data-good="down" where down is good), and a sparkline, ring or meter drops in as it is.
